name: Trestolone (MENT)

lead: Trestolone, also called MENT (7-alpha-methyl-19-nortestosterone), is an experimental synthetic androgen that was developed for male hormonal contraception and androgen replacement. It has not been approved as a medicine. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing spaces it is mentioned as a very potent androgen, sometimes called ment.

The only human research located is a registered phase 1 trial of its effects on blood pressure in normal men. On looksmax.org, one thread proposes applying transdermal androgens to the jawline for facial remodeling, a speculative idea that other users challenged and that no study supports.

paras: Grokipedia describes it as a potent androgen-receptor agonist with progestogenic activity that is not converted to DHT by 5-alpha-reductase and that suppresses gonadotropins; this is the basis for its research as a contraceptive.[1] The looksmax.org claim of local jawline binding is a forum hypothesis.[2]

Because it is unapproved, safety knowledge comes from small research studies, including a registered trial of its effect on blood pressure in 68 men.[3] Forum users anticipate acne, skin irritation and more facial hair from the topical idea, and one asked that any tester be someone not prone to acne or baldness.[2]

lead: Trestolone, known in research as MENT, is a synthetic 19-nortestosterone-type androgen with a methyl group at the 7-alpha position. According to Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, it was developed in the 1960s and later studied by the Population Council as a candidate for male hormonal contraception and androgen replacement; it has not been approved for medical use.[1]

The registered human research found is a two-part phase 1 study, completed in 2008 to 2009, with an open-label pilot and a randomized placebo-controlled part, assessing the effects of MENT on blood pressure in 68 normal men.[2] Earlier contraceptive and replacement studies are described by Grokipedia but were not independently confirmed.[1]

In looksmaxxing communities, trestolone appears as a very potent androgen. One looksmax.org thread proposes a stack of transdermal DHT, trenbolone and MENT with IGF-1 to remodel the jawline, reasoning that topical androgens would bind receptors locally; replies questioned the reasoning, noting that preventing bone breakdown differs from causing bone growth.[3] No study has tested this.
infobox: Intramuscular / implant (research); topical use discussed on forums

paras: A registered phase 1 trial (NCT00812630), begun in December 2008 and completed, examined the effect of MENT on blood pressure in normal men, first in an open-label pilot and then in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled part with 68 participants.[2] Grokipedia also describes earlier small trials in hypogonadal men and in male contraception conducted by the Population Council, reporting maintenance of lean mass, libido and hematocrit comparable to testosterone and azoospermia or severe oligospermia in a majority of men at the higher implant number; these accounts have not been verified against the primary publications here.[1] No study has examined trestolone for physique or facial appearance.

Grokipedia says trestolone was investigated for androgen replacement in hypogonadal men, delivered by subcutaneous implants, and for reversible male contraception through suppression of luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone, and that development stalled due to implant release variability and funding.[1]

A looksmax.org thread titled as an aggressive androgenic facial remodeling stack suggests applying transdermal androgens (DHT, trenbolone, MENT) with an IGF-1 analogue to the jaw. The poster argued that transdermal androgens would be absorbed locally and bind receptors in the jawline, drawing on published reports of topical DHT for micropenis in partial androgen insensitivity; he acknowledged likely side effects such as acne, irritation, more facial hair and systemic absorption.[3] One reply asked for a volunteer 'lab rat' who is not sensitive to acne or balding; another said that DHT is localised but has no noticeable effect on bone and that slowing bone breakdown is not the same as bone growth.[3] A second thread titled 'Enjoy the ment' also exists, with no content usable here.[4]

Published adverse-effect information is limited to what Grokipedia reports about the investigational program, including possible mood effects, and to the blood-pressure trial's existence.[1][2] The forum poster anticipated acne, irritation and facial hair from topical use.[3]

Grokipedia states that trestolone is a strong androgen-receptor agonist that is not 5-alpha-reduced, has progestogenic activity, is rapidly cleared after injection and may be detectable only briefly in urine.[1] These claims come from an AI-generated source and are presented here as reported.

lore.intro: Trestolone is mentioned on looksmax.org as an extremely potent androgen, with one thread proposing topical use on the jaw.[3][4]

claims.claim: Topical androgens like DHT, tren and MENT bind locally in the jawline and could remodel the face.
Androgens' effect on bone preservation implies bone growth.
MENT is a far more potent anabolic than testosterone.
